domain_setting: Everyday scenes in which people experience, evaluate, and react to food, ideas, performances, products, places, and service.
visual_thesis: Show a concrete situation plus a visible human reaction so each evaluative word is learned through its lesson-specific use rather than as an isolated symbol.
recurring_scale_anchors: 304 x 192 card with an ivory paper stage and grounded tabletop or floor
Human busts use the Artico recurring cast proportions and expressive faces
A familiar tabletop, café counter, or performance stage anchors everyday evaluation scenes
Use a muted comparison object for gradable adjectives when it clarifies the contrast

polysemy_resolution_table.brilliant: Excellent or clever in the positive-opinion lesson; do not depict literal brightness or a light bulb.
polysemy_resolution_table.fantastic: Exceptionally good or enjoyable; do not depict the unrelated sense 'strange' and distinguish the scene from breathtaking scenery.
polysemy_resolution_table.good: Positive quality or result in an everyday evaluation; do not use a moral-goodness scene or another food-taste scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.great: Very good in the positive-opinion lesson (confirmed on the live lesson page); do not use the separate size sense 'large'.
polysemy_resolution_table.incredible: So remarkable that it is hard to believe; do not use the sense 'untrustworthy'.
polysemy_resolution_table.extraordinary: Far outside the ordinary range; show an unmistakably rare scale or feature rather than generic beauty.
polysemy_resolution_table.interesting: Engaging enough to hold someone's attention, not merely unusual.
polysemy_resolution_table.odd: Unusual in a mildly unexpected way; distinguish from strange if both are pictured.
polysemy_resolution_table.favorite: The one preferred choice among alternatives, not a favorite person or celebrity.
polysemy_resolution_table.worth it: A positive judgment that the outcome justifies the effort or cost, not a literal price tag.
